title: The Hares and the Frogs
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 野兔因胆小想去投湖，却发现青蛙更怕它们，于是重拾勇气。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: IN A FOREST, deep, shady, and still, there once lived a company of Hares.
paragraphs.zh: 在一片幽深、阴凉、寂静的森林里，从前住着一群野兔。

paragraphs.en: Whenever a leaf fell rustling to the ground, or a squirrel, jumping in the branches, broke a twig, the Hares started and trembled, they were so timid.
paragraphs.zh: 每当一片叶子沙沙落地，或是一只松鼠在枝头跳跃碰断细枝，野兔们就会惊跳发抖，它们实在太胆小了。

paragraphs.en: One day there came a great wind, rushing through the tops of the trees with a roaring noise, and waving the branches back and forth.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天刮起一阵大风，呼呼地从树梢间穿过，把树枝来回摇晃。

paragraphs.en: It frightened the Hares so much that they all started together, running as fast as they could to get out of the forest, which had been their home.
paragraphs.zh: 野兔们吓坏了，于是一齐动身，拼命跑出这片一直是它们家园的森林。

paragraphs.en: “What a sad state is ours,” they said, “never to eat in comfort, to sleep always in fear, to be startled by a shadow, and fly with beating heart at the rustling of the leaves. Better death, by far. Let us drown ourselves in yonder lake.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们的处境多可怜啊，”它们说，“从不能安心吃东西，睡觉总提心吊胆，一有影子就受惊，听见叶子沙沙响就心跳着逃跑。倒不如死了好。我们到那边湖里去投水吧。”

paragraphs.en: But when they came to the lake, it happened that there were scores of frogs sporting on the banks; who, when they heard the sound of footsteps, jumped into the water.
paragraphs.zh: 可它们来到湖边时，正巧有几十只青蛙在岸上嬉戏；青蛙一听见脚步声，就跳进了水里。

paragraphs.en: The timid Hares were startled by the splash; but, as they saw the frogs dive to the bottom of the lake, a wise old Hare said, “Stop a moment! let us consider. Here are creatures that are more timid than we—they are afraid even of us. See, they are drowning themselves for fear of us! It may not be so bad with us as we thought. Perhaps we have been foolish, as foolish as the frogs, who are alarmed when there is no danger. Let us make the best of our lot, and try to be brave in it.” So back they went again to the forest.
paragraphs.zh: 胆小的野兔被扑通声吓了一跳；可当它们看见青蛙潜入湖底，一只聪明的老野兔说：“等一等！让我们想一想。这里有比我们更胆小的生灵——它们连我们都怕。看，它们因为怕我们竟要淹死自己！我们的处境也许没有想的那么糟。也许我们一直很傻，傻得像那些青蛙，明明没有危险却惊慌失措。让我们尽量把日子过好，试着勇敢一些。”于是它们又回到了森林里。
